Resolves #8890

A child that changes before its parent becomes pending can be absent from that parent's sparse allowlist. The collision filter now keeps the child's separate root unless the parent covers it by both depth and sparse membership. Dense and full-depth parents retain their existing behavior; clean siblings remain pruned. The allowlist is retained before payload creation resets the scope flags, without another tree walk or allowlist copy.

Evidence: L3 (local Chrome, real App → VDom → Main → App, dedicated and shared workers) → L3 required by the operator for this VDOM behavior change. Whole-application release acceptance remains on #14800.

## AC Evidence

No structured ACs on #8890. CI coverage in `test/playwright/unit/vdom/SparseUpdates.spec.mjs` verifies excluded and included dirty siblings, finite dense and full-depth controls, one text delta, adopted vnode state, and unchanged clean-sibling pruning. Outside-CI `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/SparseUpdatesNL.spec.mjs` adds real worker/DOM roundtrip coverage, exact applied text-delta counts, retained DOM nodes, and the next independent flight.

## Deltas from ticket

The four unit controls replace an old assertion-free baseline test. At the operator's request, eight browser E2E cases were added before final acceptance. Change class: restoration; the E2E commit changes tests only.

## Test Evidence

[Browser red/green receipt and command](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19499#issuecomment-6083157183): the exact pre-fix lifecycle fails both excluded-sibling DOM arms (B stays old), while six controls pass. The repaired lifecycle passes all eight cases using dedicated and shared App/VDom workers. This Neural Link spec requires an explicit Brain runtime and is outside Engine-only CI selection; the local receipt is required.

The excluded-sibling control fails on the unpatched candidate: zero B text deltas. The included, dense and full controls pass there.

[Outside-CI preparation profile and reproducible script](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/8890#issuecomment-6082537989): interleaved exact-method A/B on Node 24.19.0, 32/512 siblings, disjoint/sparse shapes, 101 measured samples per side. Payload bytes and emitted-root counts are unchanged. The largest median increase was 0.002376 ms; this excludes queue delay, worker transport and browser rendering.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here (Missing script, exit 1). Repository pre-commit guards passed; shared PR baseline jobs will run in CI.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #8890's body (it prescribes refining the collision filter in `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs` so a sparse parent's exclusion is checked before a disjoint child's update is deleted). On `dev` `77e3df4272`, read before the diff:
    - `executeVdomUpdate`: the collection pass, `ids = updateDepth !== 1 && !denseUpdate ? mergedChildIds : null`, and the filter `parentDepth === -1 || parentDepth > distance`;
    - `TreeBuilder.#buildTree`'s prune rule: a mounted, non-allowlisted component becomes `neoIgnore` whenever `mergedChildIds` is present and `depth !== -1`, and its subtree goes with it;
    - `VDomUpdate.getMergedChildIds`: it adds the bridge ancestors of every merged child at `distance > 1`.

    Prior-art sweep: the January sessions on sparse versus dense trees and the Leapfrog expansion rule.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The filter deletes a child root only when the parent's payload really contains that child. A dense parent (`depth -1`, `denseUpdate`, no ids) keeps today's depth rule. A sparse parent additionally requires the child in the same allowlist the payload was built with; the bridges make membership sufficient for nested children. It must not re-derive TreeBuilder's walk in a second place. Test isolation should be an excluded-dirty-sibling repro plus controls showing the included-sibling, dense and full cases still deduplicated.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches.**
    - `sparseScopes` stores the exact `ids` Set passed to `getVdomUpdatePayload`, captured before the payload resets the flags, and only for `ids && updateDepth !== -1`. Depth `-1` ignores ids in TreeBuilder, so it is correctly left dense.
    - The predicate adds `(!parentIds || parentIds.has(id))` to the unchanged depth clause.
    - My falsifier confirmed the test witnesses the defect; see Test-Evidence.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The fix ships with a red-first arm I reproduced independently, and the exploratory baseline that asserted nothing is retired instead of kept beside the real test.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge** (non-blocking, pre-existing, `hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation`):
- **The gap.** The new predicate mirrors TreeBuilder's membership rule but keeps the depth clause, and TreeBuilder's sparse inclusion does not depend on depth. An allowlisted component at or beyond the parent's depth boundary is still expanded ("Leapfrog": at `depth === 1`, `isExpandable` skips the prune and `mergedChildIds.has(id)` expands it).
- **The consequence.** For such a component the filter keeps its own root, because `parentDepth > distance` is false, while the parent's payload also carries it, so it could be emitted twice.
- **When it can occur.** Merges are allowed regardless of distance (`canMergeUpdate`, Teleportation), but a depth-1 owner sends `ids = null`. So the case needs an owner with `updateDepth >= 2` and a merged descendant at `distance >= updateDepth`.
- **The falsifier.** Your harness with `parent.updateDepth = 2` and a merged grandchild that changed its text, asserting one text delta.
- **Scope.** This is not this PR's scope. It predates the patch, and the patch is strictly safer: it never deletes a root TreeBuilder omits.
